Findings.Title: An idempotent overflow retry becomes a successful invocation
Findings.Defect: BuildPackage returns 200 for any identical saved package, including Overflow, while the invocation process treats every 200/201 as a usable package and invokes the model. The mandatory fail-the-invocation decision is therefore not invariant under retry.
Evidence: First build exceeds the mandatory budget, stores status Overflow with no items/content, and returns 422. An identical retry finds the same InputsSha256 and takes the unconditional 200 existing-package branch. The concurrent-winner branch has the same problem.

RunStatelessInvocation at stateless:1577-1596 sends 200/201 through model execution and only errors through prompt refusal/cancellation. SubmitResponse later refusing an Overflow package does not undo the answer already produced.
Findings.SpecificChange: Return the same 422 agent_context_budget_exceeded, including stored diagnostics, whenever the matching existing or winning package is Overflow; make the host success path require Built defensively. Update both contracts and diagrams and name retry-after-lost-overflow-response and concurrent-overflow cases.
Findings.Regression: Newly identified interaction between existing overflow and idempotency contracts.

Findings.Title: Submission discards the claimed evidence hash required by grading
Findings.Defect: The server-computed hash and the submitted hash have different required meanings, but only one Sha256 is stored. Submission overwrites it with the server hash, so the later deterministic grade cannot identify a submitted mismatch.
Evidence: Section 6.3 explicitly requires a submitted hash that differs from the source to make the deterministic evidence check FAIL.

AgentResponseEvidenceEntity has only Sha256 and CommitSha. Submit computes source hashes and saves evidence with those hashes. There is no submitted-hash field, immutable submission snapshot, or persisted mismatch finding. SubmissionSha256 is an irreversible fingerprint, not the missing input.

Counterexample: cite an existing file with deliberately wrong hash Hbad. Submission stores Hactual. After restart the grade compares Hactual with the file and cannot distinguish this submission from one that cited Hactual.
Findings.SpecificChange: Retain the submitted hash separately from the authoritative source hash, or retain an immutable submission snapshot/mismatch result sufficient for the later grade. Specify null and unavailable-source behavior and use the authoritative hash for staleness. Add a wrong-submitted-hash case that remains FAIL after restart; mirror entity, DTO, grade, and diagram changes.
Findings.Regression: Introduced by the R3-F10 server-computed evidence-hash fix.

Findings.Title: Two accepted evidence kinds have no deterministic verification contract
Findings.Defect: Command and Commit are accepted evidence kinds, but the complete deterministic-check list defines neither verification algorithm nor expected result for them. The text says command results are checked only by the deterministic grade, whose contract omits that check.
Evidence: The enum admits File, Requirement, Receipt, Commit, Command, SessionLogTurn. RunDeterministicGrade names per-kind checks only for File, Requirement, Receipt and SessionLogTurn.

The evidence model supplies Ref, Sha256 and CommitSha but no specified command-result representation or success/claim-validation rule. A claim whose sole evidence is Command or Commit therefore has an unspecified evidence-check set and score outcome.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define reproducible deterministic checks and required evidence fields for Command and Commit, including PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, missing/mismatched receipt or commit, workspace scope, and score contribution. Alternatively explicitly remove unsupported kinds from this effort and update all schemas. Add discriminating cases for every retained kind.
Findings.Regression: Holistic completeness finding; not a request for a new grading pipeline.

Findings.Title: HV-request creation can race terminal response changes and strand a Pending item
Findings.Defect: The R3-F7 fix filters terminal responses and closes existing items, but creation participates in no response serialization protocol. A response can become Rejected/Superseded between selection and item insertion, leaving an ungradable Pending item forever.
Evidence: Allowed interleaving: CreateHvRequest reads response R as Trusted; Reject locks R, sets Rejected, sees no open HV item, commits; CreateHvRequest saves Open request plus Pending R.

All grading then refuses R with agent_context_response_not_gradable. Repeat rejection returns unchanged. The enumerated StatusVersion/Serializable operations exclude CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, which only writes the HV request/items.
Findings.SpecificChange: Make HV creation and terminal transitions share an atomic eligibility/item-creation protocol. Define ordered response locking or serializable validation/retry across the three providers, and completion behavior if every item becomes terminal. Add forced create-versus-reject and create-versus-supersede tests; update errors and diagrams.
Findings.Regression: Residual R3-F7 under concurrency; sequential cases are repaired.

Findings.Title: Trusted response reads still bypass freshness verification
Findings.Defect: GetResponse and QueryResponses(trustedOnly=true) return stored Trusted status without evaluating freshness. The GetResponse sequence explicitly authorizes use as context solely from that status.
Evidence: After a file changes, no requirement-update trigger runs. QueryResponses restricts to status Trusted and returns it; GetResponse loads fields and returns them. Neither calls EvaluateStaleness.

R3-F10 added freshness to BuildPackage and RetrieveCandidates only. The merged FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-005 says every trusted retrieval checks freshness before returning a response, and the attached plan excludes stale responses from trusted retrieval.
Findings.SpecificChange: Apply the same freshness boundary to every surface returning content as trusted, including GetResponse and trusted/status-filtered QueryResponses, before filtering/counting/paging. Or explicitly make audit reads incapable of authorizing trusted use and provide an authoritative freshness-checked path. Update sequences and add direct get/query-after-file-change tests.
Findings.Regression: Residual R3-F10; response-only dependencies and RetrieveCandidates are addressed, but public trusted reads remain a bypass.

Findings.Title: The HV agent must submit grades after the execution that could submit them has ended
Findings.Defect: The model-grade sequence requires a completed CLI turn and the runner-copied completed rollout before the same HV execution posts its grades. No continuation or second grading-submission step is specified.
Evidence: The runner waits for turn.completed and only after reviewer completion copies the rollout. RecordModelGrade requires both completed-turn evidence and that rollout.

The sequence assigns review, final verdict, completed-runner copy, then POST grades/model to the same HV lifeline. An active single codex exec cannot have its own turn.completed receipt before returning; after it returns it cannot make another tool call.
The text explicitly makes the HV agent the caller and excludes a server grading worker/pipeline, so an unstated coordinator submission cannot silently fill this gap.
Findings.SpecificChange: Specify an executable two-step manual reviewer protocol, for example a grade-only continuation by the configured HV agent after the runner freezes the completed review receipts. Define which execution/turn supplies the immutable verdict and proof, how the continuation receives them, and retry/idempotency behavior. Keep the no-HV-pipeline scope and update the sequence/live check.
Findings.Regression: The completed-rollout requirement added for R3-F1 makes this pre-existing ordering ambiguity explicit.

Findings.Title: OpenCode session.idle is an event payload, not the specified host hook
Findings.Defect: The exact adapter contract registers/forwards a session.idle hook, but OpenCode calls event({event}) for that event. Forwarding the actual hook name event is rejected by the core mapping; registering session.idle is never invoked.
Evidence: Live Hooks declares event(input: { event: Event }): Promise<void>; the plugin implements event at plugin.ts:215 and extracts the event type from its payload. The official OpenCode plugin example likewise handles session.idle inside event.

The plan allows only chat.message/session.idle/shell.env/messages.transform for this host and says any other hook exits host_event_unknown. Its logic-free adapter cannot secretly rename/filter event.type and still satisfy the exact opaque forwarding rule.

The R3-F5 fixes for separate ToolContext, input/output transport, shell.env and output mutation are present; this remaining host-shape mismatch prevents the approved stop-equivalent from reaching the PowerShell gate.
Findings.SpecificChange: Register the real event callback and forward its opaque input as HostEvent event; put event.type/session identity routing and irrelevant-event handling in the PowerShell core. Update the binding table, ACs, descriptors if needed, and Pester fixtures to exercise the real Hooks shape and session.idle delivery.
Findings.Regression: R3-F5 is only partially resolved at the actual host boundary.

Findings.Title: Phase A process diagrams still contradict queue, failsafe, and Stop contracts

Evidence: popAll compares only total line count with total queued count. Queue [A,B] and popped lines [A,A] pass that test while failing the required per-content matching-count rule. remove(absorbed_mid_turn) sends any unique matched entry straight to delivered/write-target, without the system-kind branch used by dequeue.

DrainFailsafe activity and sequence remove a mint record on session_not_open after confirmed open. FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 requires retaining it marked final and not retried, with a warning naming the prompt.

EvaluateStopGate tests remembered server gate refusal first and blocks immediately. FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC003 explicitly excepts an already-open turn after unsupportedSince; after its close is captured, the current diagram can still block on the old refusal.
Findings.SpecificChange: Match popAll by attributable content multiplicities, branch on kind for remove, retain final mint failures with their diagnostic state, and evaluate the unsupported-session/captured-close exception before a remembered completion refusal can block. Correct response sequences and trace the existing named bridge/final-mint/unsupported-session cases through every branch.

Findings.Title: The architecture still conflates REST and MCP session-log contracts
Findings.Defect: The updated units and response sequences continue to describe REST bodies/paging as if MCP returned them, and lifecycle payload descriptions omit the live MCP field-selection boundary.
Evidence: sessionlog_dialog returns {success:true,totalDialogItems:count}; architecture:408 and the shared controller/tool sequence use {agent,sessionId,requestId,totalDialogCount}. These are different field names and envelopes.

sessionlog_query returns only {totalCount,items} and has no offset parameter. Although architecture:1475 notes the missing offset, :1777-1778 still tells an MCP caller to consume limit/offset and page until complete. It cannot retrieve a later page that way.

MCP complete/fail parses turnJson then copies an explicit subset in FinalizeLifecycleTurnToolAsync:349-369. Fields such as planFile and todoId are not copied. REST forwards the body and validates those fields; the shared full-body merge/error description does not disclose this live difference. S5 adds Phase B fields, not an approved unrelated widening of every carried field.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define each existing REST and MCP request/response/error shape separately and show surface-specific response processing. Keep MCP query limitations explicit and route paging through the typed client/REST when needed. Document the current lifecycle field whitelist plus only the Phase B additions; do not silently redesign existing routes.
Findings.Regression: Found while verifying the second holistic read corrections. The REST single-turn bodies and the bulk-only TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard placement themselves are substantially corrected.

Findings.Title: Phase 2 adopts TypeScript adapters before their permitted test runner and core exist
Findings.Defect: Phase 2 writes each TypeScript adapter in final forwarding form and must gate/merge every changed plugin repo, but those repos retain Jest and have no Pester suite until Phase 4 A9. The prerequisite TestAgentPlugins deliberately fails that state.

Keep live adapters until Phase 4 and specify non-activated contract seams/fixtures in Phases 2-3, or move a complete behavior-preserving Pester migration into an approved prerequisite. Findings.Title: The rollout still specifies a shell script outside PowerShell
